title: Core War
tagline: Write programs that fight for a computer's memory.
summary: In Core War, programs called warriors, written in an assembly language named Redcode, share the memory (the core) of a simulated computer. They take turns executing one instruction each; a warrior loses when all of its processes have died.
A. K. Dewdney introduced the game in Scientific American in 1984. Players still meet under the ICWS'94 rules, and pMARS is the simulator they use.

This is pMARS 0.9.5 in the browser: its assembler, its options on a command line, its X11 core display and its debugger cdb, with the example warriors of the package. Your warriors are kept on the server, and you can battle other players online.

original.author: A. K. Dewdney & D. G. Jones (game); Albert Ma, Na'ndor Sieben, Stefan Strack & Mintardjo Wangsaw (pMARS)
